profile.reading:
Per CoreSite's own facility page, this building, DC1, is located at 1275 K Street NW, Washington, DC 20005. CoreSite publishes 22,000-plus square feet for this facility, a notably small figure relative to CoreSite's other named buildings; the page does not clarify whether this represents total building space or only leasable colocation floor space, so this entry treats the figure as CoreSite's own stated number without inferring which. No MW capacity or opening year is stated. CoreSite lists SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance for its facilities generally.

CoreSite is a subsidiary of American Tower Corporation (NYSE: AMT), which completed its acquisition of CoreSite in late 2021; Stonepeak Partners LP separately acquired roughly 29% of American Tower's US data center business in July 2022, later increased to about 36%. CoreSite's own site describes a total portfolio of 30 data centers across 11 US markets, including Washington DC, totaling more than 4.8 million square feet, with more than 44,000 customer interconnections and 500-plus connected network providers. Washington DC's downtown K Street corridor functions as a network interconnection point for the broader Northern Virginia data center region tracked heavily elsewhere in this registry, rather than as a wholesale capacity hub in its own right.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, projecting data-center segment revenue of $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026, roughly 14.9% growth at the midpoint, and raising its full-year outlook on the strength of that performance; the company also budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026. This K Street building's small footprint relative to CoreSite's other named facilities is typical of a downtown interconnection point serving as a meet-me point for network traffic rather than a bulk colocation or wholesale campus.

reading.body:
CoreSite DC1 sits in central Washington, D.C. with 22,000 square feet of technical space. No IT capacity in megawatts or racks is published. It holds certifications for financial services work, data protection, and healthcare operations: SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA. CoreSite began operating in this market in August 2005 and is now owned by American Tower after acquisition in December 2021.

This facility is the only mapped data center in Washington, D.C. with published capacity specifications on file, though that specification is empty of power or hardware counts. The state context records zero published megawatts across all mapped facilities in D.C., placing this campus first by default in a ranking that has no meaningful incumbent. The absence of published power figures makes it impossible to estimate whether this site hosts training infrastructure, inference, or neither.

For readers assessing AI infrastructure at scale, this campus offers no data on compute capacity. The technical footprint is modest at 22,000 square feet. The certifications indicate readiness for regulated workloads but do not specify whether the facility currently serves AI applications or what share of its space is allocated to GPU-intensive work. Without published power or confirmed tenant information, this site cannot be evaluated as a constraint on or contributor to AI scaling.
